ITQAN:v4p397/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p397/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p397/r1.claim: The group that intended to mislead consists of Usayd ibn Urwa and his companions.

DAMGHANI:v1p289/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r4.claim: Ḍarr can mean diminish or reduce.
DAMGHANI:v1p289/r4.anchor: الضر النقص قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

DAMGHANI:v1p291/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p291/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p291/r7.claim: Ḍalāl can mean drawing someone away from a matter without implying unbelief; in David’s case it is deviation from obedience.
DAMGHANI:v1p291/r7.anchor: الثاني ضل استنزل عن الشىء فليس بكفر قوله تعالى في سورة النساء لهمت طائفة منهم ان يضلوك

TABATABAI:12:33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:33/r2.claim: The verse about God teaching the Prophet supports the author’s claim that infallibility is a form of knowledge that diverts a person from wrongdoing.
TABATABAI:12:33/r2.anchor: ومن الدليل على أن العصمة من قبيل العلم قوله تعالى خطابا لنبيه

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r1.claim: God’s bounty and mercy here mean that He revealed Ṭuʿmah’s guilt, stopping the clansmen’s attempt to mislead the Prophet into pardoning and interceding for their guilty kinsman.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r1.anchor: understood to mean in this context that He revealed to the Prophet the true guiltof Ṭuʿmah

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r2.claim: By revealing Ṭuʿmah’s guilt, God protected the Prophet from judgment error toward both Ṭuʿmah and the innocent accused man and preserved his ʿiṣmah from sin and moral error.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r2.anchor: He protected the Prophet from committing an error in judgment with regard to

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r3.claim: The verse repeats the moral reflexivity in 4:111: those seeking to mislead the Prophet mislead only themselves.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r3.anchor: This verse also indicates the same moral reflexivity suggested in v. 111, for in seeking to lead the Prophet astray, they misled only themselves.

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r4.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Ṭuʿmah’s advocates knew their solicitation would lead the Prophet astray: revelation in 4:105 had already warned against defending betrayers, making defense of Ṭuʿmah unacceptable to God.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r4.anchor: According to al-Ṭabarī, Ṭuʿmah’s would-be advocates knew that their attempt to solicit the Prophet’s defense of Ṭuʿmah was effectively an attempt to lead the Prophet astray

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r5.claim: Other Quran passages similarly say that those seeking to lead others astray mislead themselves and that a soul’s going astray harms none but itself.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r5.anchor: See also 3:69, where, in seeking to lead others astray, the disbelievers mislead only themselves; and 39:41, where the soul’s going astray is said to harm none but itself.

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r6.speaker: R, Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r6.claim: Some interpret God’s bounty as the Prophet’s prophethood and His mercy as special aid or, more specifically, the Prophet’s ʿiṣmah, which mainstream doctrine attributes to all prophets.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r6.anchor: some understand God’s Bounty toward the Prophet in this verse to be a reference to his prophethood; they consider His Mercy to be a reference either to the special aid He rendered to the Prophet or more specifically to the Prophet’s ʿiṣmah, or moral inerrancy (R, Ṭs, Z)

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r7.claim: Elsewhere bounty and mercy refer to revealed guidance for believers generally, which prevents serious errors of judgment; this suggests the terms here need not refer only to prophetic qualities.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r7.anchor: God’s Bounty and Mercy are used in reference to God’s revelation of a particular guidance to the believers as a whole—a guidance that similarly prevents them from making serious errors of judgment—and so does not seem to relate only to the specific qualities given to the prophets

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r8.claim: God protects the Prophet from being misled by teaching him hidden realities and people’s inner intentions, or by instructing him in religious law.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r8.anchor: In the present verse, God protects the Prophet from being led astray by teaching him what he did not know, either in the sense of revealing to him the hidden nature of affairs and the inner intentions of people or simply in the sense of instructing him in religious Law (Z)

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r9.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r9.claim: The Book refers to scripture itself, while Wisdom means religious knowledge and understanding more generally.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r9.anchor: the Book refers to the scripture itself, and Wisdom to religious knowledge and understanding more generally.

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r10.claim: The Quran also says that God granted various prophets both the Book and Wisdom.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r10.anchor: The Quran elsewhere speaks of God granting various prophets both the Book and Wisdom

STUDYQURAN:4:113/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r11.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r11.claim: Al-Rāzī takes the repeated declaration of God’s great bounty after the mention of revelation and teaching as evidence that knowledge is God’s noblest gift and virtue.
STUDYQURAN:4:113/r11.anchor: For al-Rāzī, the reiteration of the greatness of God’s Bounty, after describing His Revelation of the Book and Wisdom and His teaching the Prophet what he did not know, is a clear indication that knowledge is the “noblest of the bounties and virtues”

TAB-FULL:v7p479/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r1.claim: God's favor and guidance protected Muhammad and clarified the traitor's case, so Muhammad refrained from arguing for him or defending him against the rightful claimant.
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r1.anchor: الله تفضل عليك يا محمد فعصمك بتوفيقه وتبيانه لك أمر هذا الخائن

TAB-FULL:v7p479/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r2.claim: The faction tried to lead Muhammad from the right judgment by disguising the traitor's case, testifying that he was innocent, and asking Muhammad to excuse and defend him among his companions.
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r2.anchor: وذلك لتلبيسهم أمر الخائن عليه صلى الله عليه وسلم وشهادتهم للخائن عنده بأنه بريء مما ادعي عليه، ومسألتهم إياه أن يعذره

TAB-FULL:v7p479/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r3.claim: They misled themselves by taking a forbidden path and aiding the wrongdoer rather than the people he had wronged; God's command was to avoid aiding sin and to help what is right. The earlier prohibition on defending traitors is 4:105.
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r3.anchor: في كتابه على لسان رسوله إلى خلقه بالنهي عن أن يتعاونوا على الإثم والعدوان والأمر بالتعاون على الحق

TAB-FULL:v7p479/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r4.claim: Their attempt cannot harm Muhammad: God will strengthen and guide him, reveal their effort to mislead him, and expose both the plotters and the traitor.
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r4.anchor: لأن الله مثبتك ومسددك في أمورك ومبين لك أمر من سعوا في ضلالك عن الحق في أمره وأمرهم، ففاضحه وإياهم.

TAB-FULL:v7p479/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r5.claim: The Book is the Qur'an, containing clarification of everything, guidance, and admonition.
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r5.anchor: وهو القرآن الذي فيه بيان كل شيء، وهدى وموعظة

TAB-FULL:v7p479/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r6.claim: Wisdom is what the Book states in summary: its lawful and forbidden matters, commands and prohibitions, rulings, promises, and warnings.
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r6.anchor: هي ما كان في الكتاب مجملا ذكره

TAB-FULL:v7p479/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p479/r7.claim: God taught Muhammad accounts of earlier and later peoples and what had happened or would happen; this too is God's favor.

TAB-FULL:v7p481/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p481/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p481/r1.claim: Since God has shown Muhammad immense favor, he should thank God through obedience, hasten to God's pleasure, keep to revelation, and oppose those trying to divert him; God will protect him, while no one can save him if he disobeys and follows their desire.
TAB-FULL:v7p481/r1.anchor: فإن الله هو الذي يتولاك بفضله

TAB-FULL:v7p481/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v7p481/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v7p481/r2.claim: The verse alerts Muhammad to his own welfare and reminds him of the duty he owes God.
TAB-FULL:v7p481/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية تنبيه من الله نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم على موضع حظه، وتذكير منه له الواجب عليه من حقه

TABATABAI:4:105-109/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-109/r7.claim: The passage also establishes the Prophet's protection from error, alongside other religious truths to be discussed later.

TABATABAI:4:105-106/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r11.claim: The Prophet did not commit a consequential sin or approach a blameworthy act; he asks God to keep him from ego-driven defense of treachery, as 4:113 confirms his divine protection.
TABATABAI:4:105-106/r11.anchor: بل ليسأل من الله أن يظهره على هوى النفس

TABATABAI:4:113/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113/r4.claim: The group is the same people addressed in 4:109 for arguing on behalf of others, corresponding to the people of Abu Tuʿmah.

TABATABAI:4:113/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113/r5.claim: The group misleads only itself because its attempted action is sinful and every sin is a form of error; the misguidance does not reach the Prophet.
TABATABAI:4:113/r5.anchor: فهم الضالون بما هموا به لأنه معصية وكل معصية ضلال

TABATABAI:4:113#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r1.claim: He mentions another sense previously discussed for this phrase at 3:69 but says it does not fit the present context.

TABATABAI:4:113#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r2.claim: The apparent absolute denial of harm is restricted by the following clause about God's sending down the Book, construed as a circumstantial clause; grammarians usually expect qad before a past-tense verbal clause there.
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r2.anchor: غير أن ظاهر السياق أنه مقيد بقوله

TABATABAI:4:113#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r3.claim: In context, the clause denies that people can harm the Prophet in any respect, in knowledge or action.
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r3.anchor: وعلى هذا فالكلام مسوق لنفي إضرار الناس مطلقا بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في علم أو عمل

TABATABAI:4:113#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r4.claim: The divine revelation and teaching explains why their attempts cannot mislead or harm the Prophet: it is the basis of his infallibility.
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r4.anchor: فهذا الإنزال والتعليم هو المانع من تأثيرهم في إضلاله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم فهو الملاك في عصمته

TABATABAI:4:113#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r5.claim: The verse presents infallibility as a kind of knowledge that prevents its possessor from committing sin and error, as settled dispositions such as courage or chastity produce their effects and block opposites.
TABATABAI:4:113#2/r5.anchor: ظاهر الآية ان الأمر الذي تتحقق به العصمة نوع من العلم يمنع صاحبه عن التلبس بالمعصية والخطأ

TABATABAI:4:113#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r1.claim: Ordinary beneficial knowledge and wisdom generally keep a person from vice, but like other natural causes they do not prevent every lapse; learned and pious people can still err.
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r1.anchor: والعلم النافع والحكمة البالغة وإن كانا يوجبان تنزه صاحبهما عن الوقوع في مهالك الرذائل

TABATABAI:4:113#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r2.claim: Human faculties compete: desire can distract a pious person from awareness of piety or weaken that awareness, allowing appetite to prevail; other motivational causes work similarly.
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r2.anchor: والوجه في ذلك ان القوى الشعورية المختلفة في الإنسان يوجب بعضها ذهوله عن حكم البعض الآخر أو ضعف التفاته إليه

TABATABAI:4:113#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r3.claim: Infallibility is a cognitive cause that is never overpowered; ordinary forms of acquired awareness could sometimes fail, so this knowledge differs from them.
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r3.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن هذه القوة المسماة بقوة العصمة سبب شعوري علمي غير مغلوب البتة

TABATABAI:4:113#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r4.claim: God points to this special knowledge in His address specifically to the Prophet, saying He taught him what he had not known.
TABATABAI:4:113#3/r4.anchor: وقد أشار الله تعالى إليه في خطابه الذي خص به نبيه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r1.claim: The descent onto the Prophet's heart by Gabriel and the Trustworthy Spirit in 2:97 and 26:192–195 shows that the descent described here is a kind of knowledge and revelation.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r1.anchor: أن الإنزال المذكور من نسخ العلم

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r2.claim: Other verses describe God's communication to the Prophet as revelation, supporting the identification of this teaching with divine revelation.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r2.anchor: ويظهر من جهة أخرى أن ذلك من قبيل الوحي والتكليم

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r3.claim: The final phrase is not limited to what the Book and wisdom teach: the context concerns the Prophet's personal judgment in disputes, which depends on but is distinct from those general teachings.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r3.anchor: فإن مورد الآية قضاء النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في الحوادث الواقعة والدعاوي التي ترفع إليه برأيه الخاص

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r4.claim: The verse names two kinds of teaching: revelation through the angel, and divine inspiration or a hidden casting into the Prophet's heart without an angel's descent.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r4.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن المراد بالانزال والتعليم في

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r5.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r5.claim: Reports about the Prophet's knowledge support a second kind of divine teaching: hidden inspiration into the heart without an angel's descent.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r5.anchor: وهذا هو الذي تؤيده الروايات الواردة في علم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r6.claim: This is knowledge God gives directly; ordinary means by which people acquire knowledge would not suffice to provide it.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r6.anchor: آتاك نوعا من العلم لو لم يؤتك إياه من لدنه لم يكفك في إيتائه الأسباب العادية التي تعلم الانسان ما يكتسبه من العلوم

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r7.claim: This divine gift of infallibility is a kind of knowledge unlike ordinary knowledge: it dominates other faculties and therefore protects its possessor from error and sin absolutely.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r7.anchor: هذه الموهبة الالهية التي نسميها قوة العصمة نوع من العلم والشعور يغاير سائر انواع العلوم في أنه غير مغلوب لشيء من القوى الشعورية البتة

TABATABAI:4:113#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r8.speaker: الروايات
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r8.claim: Reports say the Prophet and Imam have a spirit called the Holy Spirit that supports and protects them from sin and error.
TABATABAI:4:113#4/r8.anchor: وقد ورد في الروايات أن للنبي والامام روحا تسمى روح القدس

TABATABAI:4:113#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r1.claim: Read literally, 42:52's Spirit from God's command is a teaching, guiding word cast to the Prophet.
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r1.anchor: بتنزيل الآية على ظاهرها من إلقاء كلمة الروح المعلمة الهادية إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:4:113#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r2.claim: On the interpretation he will later give 21:73, the verse refers to the Holy Spirit's support of the Imam in good deeds and worship.
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r2.anchor: المراد به تسديد روح القدس الامام بفعل الخيرات وعبادة الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:4:113#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r3.claim: The Book means revelation sent to resolve people's disagreements, as described generally in 2:213.
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r3.anchor: هو الوحي النازل لرفع اختلافات الناس

TABATABAI:4:113#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r4.claim: Wisdom means the other divine teachings revealed through revelation, beneficial in this life and the next.
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r4.anchor: والمراد بالحكمة سائر المعارف الالهية النازلة بالوحي

TABATABAI:4:113#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r5.claim: The phrase means knowledge beyond the general and universal teachings contained in the Book and wisdom.
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r5.anchor: غير المعارف الكلية العامة من الكتاب والحكمة

TABATABAI:4:113#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r6.claim: Some commentators identify the Book with the Qur'an, wisdom with its rulings, and the knowledge beyond it with rulings and unseen matters; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says this reading is weak.

TABATABAI:4:113#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r7.claim: Others identify the Book and wisdom with Qur'an and Sunna, and the extra knowledge with laws, histories of earlier messengers, and other sciences; he rejects this too.
TABATABAI:4:113#5/r7.anchor: وفسر بعضهم الكتاب والحكمة بالقرآن والسنة

TABATABAI:4:113-115/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:113-115/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:4:113-115/r1.claim: The statement that God's favor to the Prophet was great is an expression of benefaction.
TABATABAI:4:113-115/r1.anchor: امتنان على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r3.claim: The same al-Qummi report identifies the party who tried to mislead the Prophet as the people who went to him to defend Bashir.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#2/r3.anchor: وانزل الله في النفر الذين أعذروا بشرا وأتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ليعذروه

TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.claim: Qatada recounts that the Banu Ubayriq enlisted Usayr ibn Urwa and neighbors to accuse him and Rifa'a of slandering a pious household; the Prophet challenged Qatada for alleging theft without proof.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r1.anchor: قال قتادة فأتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فكلمته، فقال عمدت إلى أهل بيت ذكر منهم إسلام وصلاح

TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.claim: Qatada’s report glosses the “traitors” as the Banu Ubayriq, the command to seek forgiveness as concerning the Prophet’s rebuke of Qatada, the slander as their charge against Lubayd, and the party as Usayr ibn Urwa’s allies.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#3/r2.anchor: ولا تكن للخائنين خصيما - بني أبيرق - واستغفر الله - أي مما قلت لقتادة

TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd gives a variant: a thief framed a Jewish man for stealing armor, whose neighbors defended the thief and disparaged the Jew; revelation rebuked their defense, offered repentance, and the thief later died when a house he tried to rob collapsed.
TABATABAI:4:105-126#4/r3.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن زيد في الآية قال كان رجل سرق درعا من حديد

TABRISI:4:113-114/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114/r2.claim: Hamm is what one intends or resolves to do; related words include himma (aspiration) and hammām (a king of great aspiration).
TABRISI:4:113-114/r2.anchor: الهم ما هممت به ومنه الهمة

TABRISI:4:113-114/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114/r14.claim: God's favor and mercy turned the group's plotting away from His Messenger and protected him from inclining toward them.
TABRISI:4:113-114/r14.anchor: لطفه برسوله وفضله عليه إذ صرف كيدهم عنه

TABRISI:4:113-114/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114/r15.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:113-114/r15.claim: One gloss identifies God's favor as prophethood and His mercy as support through revelation.
TABRISI:4:113-114/r15.anchor: { فضل الله } النبوة { ورحمته } نصرته إياه بالوحي

TABRISI:4:113-114/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114/r16.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:4:113-114/r16.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī instead explains favor as God's support through subtle acts of grace and mercy as His blessing.
TABRISI:4:113-114/r16.anchor: تأييده بألطافه { ورحمته } نعمته عن الجبائي

TABRISI:4:113-114/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114/r17.speaker: ابن عباس، الحسن، الجبائي
TABRISI:4:113-114/r17.claim: They identify the group as those who testified that the Banū Ubairiq traitors were innocent, trying to turn the Prophet from the truth; God exposed their secrets.
TABRISI:4:113-114/r17.anchor: بالبراءة عن ابن عباس والحسن والجبائي

TABRISI:4:113-114/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:4:113-114/r18.claim: A second identification makes the group the Thaqīf delegation, which had asked the Prophet for an impermissible concession.
TABRISI:4:113-114/r18.anchor: الذين التمسوا من رسول الله ما لا يجوز وقد مضى ذكرهم عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:4:113-114/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114/r19.claim: A third reading takes the group as hypocrites who intended to kill and destroy the Prophet; here making someone go astray means killing them, as in 32:10.
TABRISI:4:113-114/r19.anchor: أنهم المنافقون الذين هموا بإهلاك النبي والمراد بالإضلال

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r1.claim: He compares misguidance used for killing with 32:10 and notes the parallel that the hypocrites intended what they did not attain in 9:74.

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r2.claim: They turn only themselves from the truth; an alternative gloss is that they bring destruction on themselves and incur everlasting punishment.
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r2.anchor: وما يزيلون عن الحق إلا أنفسهم

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r3.claim: Their scheming cannot harm the Prophet because God protects, helps, guides, and supports him.
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r3.anchor: أي لا يضرونك بكيدهم ومكرهم شيئا

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r4.claim: The Book and Wisdom are the Qur'an and Sunna; they could not mislead him while God revealed the Book and rulings to him.
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r4.anchor: أي القرآن والسنة واتصاله بما قبله

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r5.claim: God taught the Prophet laws, accounts of earlier messengers, and other knowledge he had not known.
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r5.anchor: أي ما لم تعلمه من الشرائع وأنباء الرسل الأولين

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r6.claim: One gloss says God's favor was immense from the Prophet's creation onward: He made him the last prophet and chief of messengers and granted him intercession and more.
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r6.anchor: فضله عليك منذ خلقك إلى أن بعثك عظيم

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r12.claim: The verse shows that a sinner harms himself through the consequence of his own deed, and that one who invites to misguidance misleads others and himself.
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r12.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على أن فاعل المعصية هو الذي يضر بنفسه

TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r13.claim: Calling the inviter to misguidance a misleader, and calling its perpetrator a misleader of himself, shows that inviting to error is itself called misguidance.
TABRISI:4:113-114#2/r13.anchor: وفيها دلالة أيضا على أن الذي يدعو إلى الضلال هو المضل

THALABI:v3p383#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p383#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p383#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies God's favor and mercy as Islam and the Qurʾan, and says a group from Thaqif tried to lead Muhammad astray.
THALABI:v3p383#2/r1.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس، ثم قال: ولولا فضل الله. عليك ورحمته يعني به الإسلام والقرآن لهمت طائفة

THALABI:v3p383#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p383#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p383#2/r2.claim: The Thaqif delegation offered allegiance only if there were no resurrection, they could keep their idols, and they could honor al-ʿUzza for a year; Muhammad refused, and God protected him.
THALABI:v3p383#2/r2.anchor: وذلك أن وفد ثقيف قدموا على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: يا محمد قد جئناك نبايعك

THALABI:v3p383#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p383#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p383#2/r3.claim: The plotters harm only themselves; they cannot strip Muhammad of prophethood, since God made him worthy of it.
THALABI:v3p383#2/r3.anchor: فقال وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم يعني وفد ثقيف وما يضرونك من شيء يعني لا يستطيعون أن يزيلوا عنك النبوة

THALABI:v3p383#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p383#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v3p383#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the Book and Wisdom as the rulings, and what Muhammad was taught as the religious ordinances.
THALABI:v3p383#2/r4.anchor: ثم قال وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة يعني الأحكام وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم من الشرائع

THALABI:v3p383#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p383#2/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p383#2/r5.claim: The great divine favor bestowed on Muhammad is faith.
THALABI:v3p383#2/r5.anchor: وكان فضل الله أي من الله عليك بالإيمان عظيما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, identifies God's favor and mercy as prophethood and protection from sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: بالنبوة والعصمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the favor as prophethood and God's support of the Prophet through revelation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj take the counterfactual wording to mean the faction did in fact intend and conceal its plan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء والزجاج: المعنى: لقد همت فأضمرت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r4.claim: The faction is Ṭuʿma's party: some knew he had stolen the armor but still asked the Prophet to argue for him and blame the Jew.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r4.anchor: لأن بعضهم قد كان وقف على أنه سارق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj glosses their attempt to mislead the Prophet as making him err in judgment.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r6.claim: They mislead only themselves by cooperating in sin and aggression and giving false testimony.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r6.anchor: بتعاونهم على الإثم والعدوان، وشهادتهم بالزور والبهتان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says their own actions are the actions of people who have gone astray.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج: لأنهم يعملون عمل الضالين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r8.claim: The harm of false testimony falls on those who testify without right, not on the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r8.anchor: لأن الضر على من شهد بغير حق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r9.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj attributes the Prophet's immunity from harm to God's protection and support for the true religion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p84#2/r9.anchor: مع عصمة الله إياك، ونصرة (¬6) دين الحق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r1.claim: The waw may begin a new statement of divine favor or introduce a circumstantial clause with an implicit qad, as in 4:90.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r2.claim: The Book is the Quran and wisdom is judgment by revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r2.anchor: والمراد بالكتاب: القرآن، وبالحكمة القضاء بالوحي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq says God clarified in the Book its wisdom, which prevents the Prophet from straying.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p85/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: أي بين لك في كتابه ما فيه من الحكمة

QASHANI:4:113-114/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:113-114/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:113-114/r1.claim: God's favor is enabling support on the spiritual path that actualizes the Prophet's latent perfection and knowledge.
QASHANI:4:113-114/r1.anchor: توفيقه وإمداده لسلوك طريقه بما يخرج كمالك إلى الفعل ويبرز ما فيك كامنا من العلم

QASHANI:4:113-114/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:113-114/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:113-114/r2.claim: The mercy is God's gift of the absolute perfection deposited in the Prophet from eternity, a mercy beyond which none is possible.
QASHANI:4:113-114/r2.anchor: هبته لذلك الكمال المطلق الذي أودعه فيك في الأزل وهي الرحمة التي ليس وراءها رحمة

QASHANI:4:113-114/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:113-114/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:113-114/r3.claim: The plotters mislead only themselves because misguidance arises from their primordial disposition toward wretchedness and cannot transfer to another.
QASHANI:4:113-114/r3.anchor: لكون الضلال ناشئا من أصل استعدادهم لكونهم مجبولين على الشقاوة أزلا

QASHANI:4:113-114/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:113-114/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:113-114/r4.claim: The Book is complete, detailed knowledge after gifted existence; wisdom is knowledge of detailed rulings and attribute-manifestations together with acting upon them.
QASHANI:4:113-114/r4.anchor: علم أحكام التفاصيل وتجليات الصفات مع العمل به

QASHANI:4:113-114/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:113-114/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:113-114/r5.claim: God alone knows His own knowledge; after unveiling His essence through annihilation and restoring the Prophet in true existence, the Prophet's heart knows with God's knowledge, since attributes follow essence.
QASHANI:4:113-114/r5.anchor: فلما كشف لك عن ذاته بفنائك فيه ثم أبقاك بالوجود الحقاني فصار قلبك وحجبك بحجاب ذلك القلب علمك علمه

QASHANI:4:113-114/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:4:113-114/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:4:113-114/r6.claim: God's great favor is manifesting this perfection through the practice that brought the Prophet to his attained state.
QASHANI:4:113-114/r6.anchor: في إظهار هذا الكمال عليك بالتوفيق للعمل الذي أوصلك إلى ما أوصلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r5.claim: God's favor and mercy toward the Prophet mean prophethood and protection from error.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r5.anchor: { ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته } بالنبوة والعصمة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r6.claim: Tuʿma's people tried to lead the Prophet into a mistaken judgment by asking him to defend them and condemn the Jew.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r6.anchor: أي: يخطئوك في الحكم، وذلك أنهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يجادل عنهم ويقطع اليهودي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r7.claim: They mislead only themselves through collaboration in sin, aggression, false testimony, and slander.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r7.anchor: { وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم } بتعاونهم على الإثم والعدوان وشهادتهم الزور والبهتان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r8.claim: The person harmed is the one who testifies falsely.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r8.anchor: { وما يضرونك من شيء } لأن الضرر على من شهد بغير حق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r9.claim: God gave the Prophet scripture and wisdom, meaning judgment through revelation, and showed its wisdom.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:4:112-114/r9.anchor: { وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة } أي: القضاء بالوحي، وبين لك ما فيه الحكمة

ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r12.claim: Tuʿma’s people knew he was the thief, yet came to defend him, secure his acquittal, and shift the theft onto a Jew.
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r12.anchor: Tu‘me’nin kavmi onun sârık olduğunu bildikleri hâlde Peygamber’e gelmişler

ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r13.claim: Their cooperation in sin, false testimony, and slander misguides only themselves and does the Prophet no harm.
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r13.anchor: ve yalan yere şehâdet ve bühtan ile kendilerini dalâlete düşürüyorlar

ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r14.claim: The Prophet would judge according to outward circumstances; a judge is not liable for a false result when contrary facts are neither known nor established.
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r14.anchor: sen hükmünü zâhir-i hâle binâ edecektin

ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r15.claim: God’s favor here is the gift of prophethood, while His mercy is the Prophet’s preservation and protection from error.
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r15.anchor: nübüvveti ve rahmeti, yani hıfz u ismeti olmasa idi

ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r16.claim: The revealed Book is a proof above every other proof, and wisdom is the foremost quality for correctness in knowledge and action.
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r16.anchor: Kitab her delîlin fevkinde bir delil; hikmet, ilm ü amelde hakk u savâba isabet için en büyük bir haslet

ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r17.claim: Divinely given inward knowledge reveals realities beyond appearances and preserves the Prophet from error and harm.
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r17.anchor: bu ilm-i ledün zavâhirin mâverâsını gösteren ve zâhir u bâtında hatâdan

ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r18.claim: By this great favor, the Prophet judges with comprehensive prophethood and leadership, protected from error outwardly and inwardly.
ELMALILI:4:107-116#2/r18.anchor: zâhir u bâtında hatâdan ma‘sum olarak hükmedersin

QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r9.claim: God's grace signifies special protection of the Prophet from neglecting God's rights and from people's schemes.
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r9.anchor: والإشارة ههنا - من الفضل - إلى عصمته إياه

QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r10.claim: No one can lead the Prophet astray or harm him: he is held within divine might, and one God preserves is guarded from every other.
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r10.anchor: كلا ، لن يكون لأحد سبيل إلى إضلالك فأنت في قبضة العزة ، وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم ، وما يضرونك بشيء

QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r11.claim: God specially chose the Prophet to receive the Book and taught him what he did not know; no gift compares with this knowledge.
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r11.anchor: إذ المحفوظ منا محروس عن كل غير ، وإن الله سبحانه قد اختصك بإنزال الكتاب

QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r12.claim: One reading says this knowledge was of God and His majesty, and of the Prophet's servanthood and standing before divine majesty.
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أنه أراد به علمه - - بالله وبجلاله

QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r13.claim: Another reading says God taught him the manners of service and removed confusion about knowing the Real.
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r13.anchor: ويقال علمك ما لم تكن تعلم من آداب الخدمة إذ لم تكن ملتبسا عليك معرفة الحقيقة

QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r14.claim: Another reading says all people borrow their light from the Prophet, and those outside his banner miss divine goodness and nearness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p223/r14.anchor: ويقال أغناك عن تعليم الأغيار حتى لا يكون لأحد نور إلا مقتبسا من نورك

QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r1.claim: God's favor extends through eternity: the Prophet was known to God in pre-eternity with honor of might and Lordship.
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r1.anchor: في الآباد ؛ أنك كنت - لنا بشرف العز وكرم الربوبية في الآزال - معلوما

QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r2.claim: One reading of the knowledge granted is awareness of the Prophet's rank above all others.
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r2.anchor: ويقال وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم من علو رتبتك على الكافة

QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r3.claim: Another reading is that no one can know God's measure except in proportion to conformity with His command.
QUSHAYRI:v1p224/r3.anchor: أن أحدا لا يقدر قدرنا إلا بمقدار موافقته لأمرنا

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r1.claim: Divinely protected in conveying, teaching, and applying religion, the Prophet cannot be misled; those who try to mislead or harm him only harm and mislead themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r1.anchor: Yukarıda açıklandığı üzere dinin tebliği yani doğru olarak ümmete ulaştırılması, öğretilmesi ve hayatlarında uygulanması konusunda –ilâhî koruma altında bulunan– Hz. Peygamber yanılmaz.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r2.claim: The Book and Wisdom come from God rather than the Prophet’s own human knowledge; the Book is unanimously understood as the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r2.anchor: Kitap da hikmet de onun kendinden, beşerî bilgi kaynağından değil, Allah’tandır. Kitaptan maksadın Kur’an olduğunda ittifak vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r3.claim: One interpretation of Wisdom is the Qur’an’s non-legal content, which brings useful knowledge for religion and worldly life.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r3.anchor: Kur’an’ın ahkâm âyetleri dışında kalan, din ve dünya için faydalı bilgiler getiren kısmıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r4.claim: A second interpretation of Wisdom is the Sunnah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r4.anchor: din ve dünya için faydalı bilgiler getiren kısmıdır. 2. Sünnettir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r5.claim: A third interpretation of Wisdom is the ability to understand and apply revelation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r6.claim: A fourth interpretation of Wisdom is the Prophet’s distinctive mental constitution and capacity for reflection.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r6.anchor: 4. Hz. Peygamber’e mahsus zihnî yapı ve tefekkür kabiliyetidir (ayrıca bk. Bakara 2/269).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r7.claim: Before revelation, the Prophet did not know some matters about religion or the world’s past, present, and future; God later taught them to him through revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r7.anchor: Hz. Peygamber vahiy gelmeden önce gerek din ve gerekse dünyanın geçmişi, o günü ve geleceği konusunda bilmediği bazı şeyleri sonradan vahiy yoluyla Allah’tan öğrenmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r8.claim: God bestowed great favors and exceptional qualities on His beloved Prophet, and the community and all humanity have benefited and continue to benefit from some of them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:113/r8.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, sevgili peygamberine büyük lutuflarda bulunmuş, müstesna özellikler bahşetmiştir. Bunların bir kısmından onun ümmeti ve bütün insanlık da istifade etmiştir

BURHAN:v3p184/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p184/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p184/r4.claim: The surface reading appears to deny that the group intended to mislead the Prophet, contrary to the account that they did intend it and advanced their claim.
BURHAN:v3p184/r4.anchor: فإنه قد قيل ظاهره نفى وجود الهم منهم بإضلاله وهو خلاف الواقع فإنهم هموا وردوا القول

BURHAN:v3p184/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p184/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p184/r5.claim: An alternative analysis takes ‘they intended’ as a preposed oath-like statement, with the conditional answer omitted: without God’s favor, they would have misled you.
BURHAN:v3p184/r5.anchor: ليس جواب لو بل هو كلام تقدم على لو وجوابها مقول على طريق القسم

BURHAN:v3p91/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p91/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p91/r3.claim: The source identifies ‘wisdom’ as beneficial knowledge and righteous action, and presents the named wisdom as an explicit rationale or purpose marker.
BURHAN:v3p91/r3.anchor: والحكمة هي العلم النافع والعمل الصالح

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says direct encounter enabled the Prophet to bear the divine Essence after bearing the Attributes, whereas Moses bore the Attributes but not the Essence.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : إنما عظمت بالمباشرة فاحتمل الذات بعد ما احتمل الصفات

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r2.claim: Someone says the Prophet was favored pre-eternally yet may stumble in the witnessed moment; after reproach, as in 9:43, he returns to the favor decreed for him before time.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : فضلت في الأزل بالفضائل وقد تغتر في المشاهد العثرة

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r3.claim: Junayd glosses the teaching as making the Prophet know his own worth.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r3.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : عرفك قدر نفسك

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r4.claim: Junayd divides knowledge into gnosis, expression, servanthood, and service, and says the Prophet received their greatest share.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r4.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : عرفك قدر نفسك وقال أيضا : العلوم أربعة

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r5.speaker: أبو يزيد
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r5.claim: Abu Yazid divides knowledge into explanatory knowledge and knowledge of proof.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r5.anchor: قال أبو يزيد : العلم علمان : علم بيان وعلم برهان

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r6.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r6.claim: Sahl distinguishes believers who know God but not His commands or days, scholars who know God and His commands but not His days, and prophets and truthful ones who know all three.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r6.anchor: قال سهل : العلماء ثلاثة : عالم بالله لا عالم بأمر الله ولا بأيام الله

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r7.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r7.claim: One gloss says God taught the Prophet hidden secrets known only through God Himself.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r7.anchor: وقيل : علمتك من مكنون أسراري ما لم تعلمه إلا بي

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r8.speaker: أبو محمد الجريري
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r8.claim: Abu Muhammad al-Jurayri says scholars see outward features and excellences, sages see inward features and defects, and spiritual elders see essences and realities.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r8.anchor: وقال أبو محمد الجريري : الأدلة ثلاثة

SULAMI:v1p159#6/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r9.claim: Another classification names four scholars by their share: God Himself, knowledge and gnosis of God, the journey to the afterlife, or knowledge of that journey.
SULAMI:v1p159#6/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : العلماء أربعة : عالم حظه من الله الله

DAMGHANI:v1p359/r9.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p359/r9.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p359/r9.claim: Faḍl can mean prophethood; the source groups this with the great favor granted in the Night Journey passage.
DAMGHANI:v1p359/r9.anchor: وكان فضل الله عليك عليك عظيما يعني النبوة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r1.claim: Ḍalāl means confusion and departure from what is right; ḍalāl and ḍalāla are synonymous, and the verb has two forms.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r1.anchor: الضلال : الحيرة والعدول عن الصواب يقال : ضل يضل ويضل ، لغتان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r2.claim: Ḍalīl or muḍallal describes someone characterized by error; aḍalla can mean burying the dead.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r2.anchor: ورجل ضليل ومضلل ، صاحب ضلالة . ويقال : أضل الميت : إذا دفن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r3.speaker: ابن السكيت
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r3.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says aḍlaltu baʿīrī means my camel went missing; ḍalaltu the mosque or house means I could not find it.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r3.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : ( تقول ) : أضللت بعيري ، إذا ذهب منك . وضللت المسجد والدار

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r4.claim: Here ḍalāl means leading someone astray in judgment; the source compares 38:26.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضلال في القرآن على عشرة أوجه : أحدها : الاستذلال في الحكم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r5.claim: The verse concerns Tuʿma ibn Abayriq: after he hid stolen armor with a Jew, his people urged the Prophet to defend him and implicate the Jew; the Prophet nearly did so before revelation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r5.anchor: نزلت في أمر طعمة بن أبيرق . وكان قد سرق درعا وتركها عند يهودي

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضلال في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضلال في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضلال في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r9.claim: Ḍalāl means futility or being nullified in 18:103 and 47:1.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p406/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الضلال في القرآن على عشرة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r1.claim: Wisdom is a kind of knowledge that prevents a person from undertaking falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r1.anchor: قال بعض أهل العلم : الحكمة : ضرب من العلم يمنع من ركوب الباطل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r2.claim: Another definition is the soul's attainable perfection in knowledge and action, culminating in justice; a horse's rein is called ḥikma because it restrains the animal, as wisdom restrains its possessor.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r2.anchor: وقال غيره : الحكمة : خروج نفس الإنسان إلى كمالها الممكن لها في حدي العلم ، والعمل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r3.claim: Wisdom is knowledge and action together; a person is not wise without both.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r3.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : الحكمة : العلم ، والعمل ، لا يكون الرجل حكيما حتى يجمعهما

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r4.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r4.claim: The root ḥ-k-m means restraint; aḥkamtu or ḥakkamtu the fool means I restrained him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r4.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : أصل الحكم المنع . وأحكمت السفيه وحكمته أخذت على يده

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r5.speaker: جرير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r5.claim: Jarir's verse asks the Banu Hanifa to restrain their fools and thereby illustrates the root's sense of restraint.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r5.anchor: وقال جرير : - أبني حنيفة أحكموا سفهاءكم … إني أخاف عليكم أن أغضبا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحكمة في القرآن على ستة أوجه : - أحدها : الموعظة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r7.claim: Ḥikma means the Sunna in 2:129, 2:231, and 4:113.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r7.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحكمة في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r8.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r8.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحكمة في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r9.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحكمة في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r10.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحكمة في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r11.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p260/r11.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن الحكمة في القرآن على ستة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r1.claim: Qawl and kalam are equivalent in ordinary usage; maqūl means the tongue, and qawla or qawwāl describes someone who speaks much.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r1.anchor: القول والكلام ، واحد . والمقول : اللسان . ورجل قولة وقوال : كثير القول

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r2.claim: Some distinguish them by saying every meaningful kalam is qawl, but an uninformative sequence such as “stood, sat” is qawl but not kalam; ʿAmr al-Thumayni points to this distinction.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r2.anchor: وقد فرق قوم بين القول والكلام ، فقالوا : كل كلام قول . وليس كل قول كلاما

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r3.speaker: محمد بن القاسم النحوي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r3.claim: Qawl can mean to think or suppose, as in the Arab examples and two cited poems.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r4.speaker: أبو زكريا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r4.claim: In the clearest Arabic usage qawl does not govern the following clause overtly; with an interrogative and second-person address it can govern accusative like ẓann (think).
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r4.anchor: وقال أبو زكريا : أفصح مذاهب العرب في القول : أن لا يعمل في الجملة التي بعده في اللفظ

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القول في القرآن على خمسة أوجه : - أحدها : القرآن

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r6.claim: Qawl means the two testimonies in 14:27.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r6.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القول في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r7.claim: Qawl means what has been decreed in prior knowledge in 32:13.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r7.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القول في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p486/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن القول في القرآن على خمسة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r1.claim: In the eighth listed sense, raḥma means favor or blessing, as in 4:113 and 18:65.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r1.anchor: والثامن : النعمة . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r2.claim: Raḥma means well-being or safety in 39:38.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r2.anchor: والتاسع : العافية . ومنه قوله تعالى في الزمر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r3.claim: Raḥma means victory or deliverance in 33:17.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r3.anchor: والعاشر : النصر . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأحزاب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r4.claim: Raḥma means grace or favor in 28:46.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r4.anchor: والحادي عشر : المنة . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r5.anchor: والثاني عشر : الرقة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحديد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r6.anchor: والثالث عشر : المغفرة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأنعام

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r7.claim: Raḥma means spacious relief or easing in 2:178.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r7.anchor: والرابع عشر : السعة . ومنه قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r8.claim: Raḥma means affection or love in 48:29.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r8.anchor: والخامس عشر : المودة . ومنه قوله تعالى في الفتح

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r9.claim: Raḥma means protection from wrongdoing in 12:53.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p333/r9.anchor: والسادس عشر : العصمة . ومنه قوله تعالى في يوسف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r1.claim: Faḍl originally means increase; figurative uses depend on context.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r1.anchor: الفضل : في الأصل : الزيادة . ويستعار في مواضع

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r3.claim: The concluding phrase refers to the favor of prophethood.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r3.anchor: والثاني : الإنعام بالنبوة . ومنه قوله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r7.claim: The opening clause exemplifies faḍl as benefaction and blessing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p471/r7.anchor: والسادس : المنة والنعمة ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

FARRA:v1p287/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p287/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p287/r1.claim: La-hammat ṭāʾifa has an elided la-qad: ‘a group certainly intended.’

FARRA:v1p287/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p287/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p287/r2.claim: An yuḍillūka means to make you err in your judgment.

NAHHAS:v1p487/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p487/r1.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p487/r1.claim: For Sibawayh, the phrase after lawlā is a subject with an unexpressed predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p487/r1.anchor: ما بعد لولا مرفوع بالابتداء عند سيبويه والخبر محذوف لا يظهر

NAHHAS:v1p487/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p487/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p487/r2.claim: God’s favor and mercy mean that He alerted the Prophet to the truth.
NAHHAS:v1p487/r2.anchor: والمعنى ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته بأن نبهك على الحق

NAHHAS:v1p487/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p487/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p487/r3.claim: The group tried to mislead the Prophet after asking him to clear Ibn Ubayriq and shift the accusation to a Jew; God instead made the truth clear.
NAHHAS:v1p487/r3.anchor: لأنهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يبرىء ابن أبيرق من التهمة

NAHHAS:v1p487/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p487/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p487/r4.claim: They only mislead themselves by acting like the misguided, while God protects His Messenger.
NAHHAS:v1p487/r4.anchor: لأنهم يعملون عمل الضالين والله جل وعز يعصم رسوله

NAHHAS:v1p487/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p487/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p487/r5.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet because he is protected.
NAHHAS:v1p487/r5.anchor: ( وما يضرونك من شيء ) لأنك معصوم

NAHHAS:v1p487/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p487/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p487/r6.claim: The nūn’s ḍamma is omitted for jussive mood, wāw drops when quiescent letters meet, and taʿlamu is the predicate of takun.
NAHHAS:v1p487/r6.anchor: حذفت الضمة من النون للجزم وحذفت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين

SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r1.claim: The more evident parse has an expressed answer to lawlā: la-hammat.
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r1.anchor: في جواب " لولا " وجهان، أظهرهما: أنه مذكور وهو قوله: " لهمت "

SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r2.claim: The alternative omits the answer, estimating la-aḍallūka, and treats la-hammat as a new sentence; Abū al-Baqāʾ compares 24:10.
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه محذوف أي: لأضلوك، ثم استأنف جملة فقال: " لهمت " أي: لقد همت. قال أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r3.claim: Those who treat la-hammat as the answer address the apparent implication that their intention did not occur, despite reports that they did intend harm, by specifying an ineffective intention or misguidance from religion and law; neither occurred.
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r3.anchor: لأن اللفظ يقتضي انتفاء همهم بذلك،

SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r4.claim: The preposition bāʾ is omitted before an yuḍillūka; the clause’s case then follows the familiar grammatical disagreement.
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r4.anchor: و " ان يضلونك " على حذف الباء أي: بأن يضلوك، ففي محلها الخلاف المشهور

SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r5.claim: Min is extra, and shayʾ refers to harm of any degree, little or great.
SAMIN-DURR:4:112-113#2/r5.anchor: و " من " في " من شيء " زائدة، و " شيء " يراد به المصدر أي: وما يضرونك ضررا قليلا ولا كثيرا

ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r1.claim: The faction is Ṭuʿma's supporters; some knew he was the thief but asked the Prophet to excuse him.
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r1.anchor: والطائفة هم طعمة هذا السارق، لأن بعضهم قد كان وقف على أنه سارق، وسأل النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن يعذره.

ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r2.claim: Without God's favor and mercy in revealing the theft, the faction would nearly have misled the Prophet; God turned him from their intended course.
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r2.anchor: لولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته بما أوحى إليك. وأعلمك أمر هذا السارق لهمت طائفة أن يضلوك،

ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r3.claim: Some interpret mislead you as causing you to err in judgment.
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم معنى " أن يضلوك " أن يخطئوك في حكمك.

ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r4.claim: Their misguidance falls back on them because they act like the misguided, while God protects His Prophet from following them.
ZAJJAJ:v2p103#2/r4.anchor: أي لأنهم هم يعملون عمل الضالين. والله يعصم نبيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - من متابعتهم. والإضلال راجع عليهم وواقع بهم.

ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r1.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet at all because God protects him and supports the true religion.
ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r1.anchor: أي مع عصمة الله إياك، ونصره دينه دين الحق.

ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r2.claim: God clarified in the Book wisdom that prevents the Prophet from going astray.
ZAJJAJ:v2p104/r2.anchor: أي بين في كتابه ما فيه الحكمة التي لا يقع لك معها ضلال.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.claim: Because inspiration can mean ordinary ilham to Moses’ mother, the bee, or humans and jinn, “علمه شديد القوى” identifies Gabriel as the revealer who taught Muhammad; God remains the ultimate teacher.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p52/r1.anchor: فأراد سبحانه أن يقطع أي فكرة فقال (علّمه شديد القوى) بمعنى أنه ليس إلهاماً ولكنه وحي علّمه إياه شديد القوى

NASHR:v1p445#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445#2/r1.speaker: جماعة من أهل الأداء
NASHR:v1p445#2/r1.claim: A group including al-Dani, Faris ibn Ahmad, Makki, Ibn Shurayh, and al-Shatibi follows the official codex spelling when Hamza eases hamza at a pause.
NASHR:v1p445#2/r1.anchor: ذهب إليه جماعة من أهل الأداء كالحافظ أبي عمرو الداني، وشيخه أبي الفتح فارس بن أحمد

NASHR:v1p445#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445#2/r2.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v1p445#2/r2.claim: Sulaim reports that Hamza follows the Uthmani rasm when pausing on hamza, selecting a permissible easing that matches the written form even when another form is more analogical.
NASHR:v1p445#2/r2.anchor: أن سليما روى عن حمزة أنه كان يتبع في الوقف على الهمز خط المصحف

NASHR:v1p445#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p445#2/r3.claim: Al-Dani’s “without analogy” means without analogy detached from the codex; following the rasm cannot license a form that violates Arabic grammar. Hamza’s written shape reflects its easing, while initial hamza remains alif.
NASHR:v1p445#2/r3.anchor: فإن اتباع الرسم لا يجوز إذا خالف قياس العربية كما بينا ونبين

NASHR:v1p445#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p445#2/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p445#2/r4.claim: In the Arabic spelling principle described here, hamza eased toward alif, yā, or wāw is written accordingly; forms transferred or assimilated are omitted unless hamza is initial, when it is always written alif.
NASHR:v1p445#2/r4.anchor: فإن كان تخفيفها ألفا، أو كالألف كتبت ألفا، وإن كان ياء أو كالياء كتبت ياء

NASHR:v2p123/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p123/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p123/r1.claim: Rūm and ishām may accompany pause on a word whose connected form has a ḍamma, except when the ḍamma was transferred from another word or arose to resolve two consonants; the category includes inflection, fixed endings, and internal transfer.
NASHR:v2p123/r1.anchor: وهو ما كان في الوصل متحركا بالضم ما لم تكن الضمة منقولة من كلمة أخرى، أو لالتقاء الساكنين

NASHR:v2p123/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p123/r3.speaker: كثير من أهل الأداء
NASHR:v2p123/r3.claim: Many performance authorities allow signaling the vowel of the pronoun hāʾ without restriction; this is also the choice of Ibn Mujahid and appears in several manuals.
NASHR:v2p123/r3.anchor: ذهب كثير من أهل الأداء إلى الإشارة فيها مطلقا، وهو الذي في التيسير، والتجريد، والتلخيص، والإرشاد والكفاية، وغيرها

NASHR:v2p123/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p123/r4.speaker: آخرون
NASHR:v2p123/r4.claim: Other authorities forbid rūm and ishām on the pronoun hāʾ in every case because its vowel is incidental; this is the apparent position of al-Shatibi.
NASHR:v2p123/r4.anchor: ذهب آخرون إلى منع الإشارة فيها مطلقا من حيث إن حركتها عارضة، وهو ظاهر كلام الشاطبي

NASHR:v2p123/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p123/r5.speaker: الداني
NASHR:v2p123/r5.claim: Al-Dani records both positions as sound, while his Jamiʿ al-bayan says allowing the signal is more analogical because the pronoun is like other fixed inflections.
NASHR:v2p123/r5.anchor: وقال: الوجهان جيدان. وقال في جامع البيان: إن الإشارة إليها كسائر المبني اللازم من الضمير، وغيره أقيس

NASHR:v2p123/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p123/r6.speaker: جماعة من المحققين
NASHR:v2p123/r6.claim: A detailed position forbids signaling after a matching ḍamma, silent wāw, kasra, or silent yāʾ to avoid heaviness, but permits it elsewhere to clarify the vowel; examples include “منه” and “هداه.”
NASHR:v2p123/r6.anchor: ذهب جماعة من المحققين إلى التفصيل فمنعوا الإشارة بالروم، والإشمام فيها إذا كان قبلها ضم، أو واو ساكنة، أو كسرة، أو ياء ساكنة

IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r1.claim: Khadija and Abu Talib died in the same year, three years before the Hijra; she had supported the Prophet's Islam, and Abu Talib had protected and defended him.
IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ثم إن خديجة بنت خويلد وأبا طالب هلكا في عام واحد

IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r2.speaker: عروة بن الزبير
IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r2.claim: After Abu Talib's death Quraysh abused Muhammad more openly; Urwa reports that a man threw dirt on him, his daughter washed it away in tears, and he reassured her that God would protect him.
IBNHISHAM:v1p416/r2.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: فحدثني هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه عروة بن الزبير، قال: لما نثر ذلك السفيه

IBNHISHAM:v1p419/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p419/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p419/r1.claim: After Abu Talib died and Quraysh increased its abuse, Muhammad went alone to al-Taif seeking Thaqif's support and protection, hoping they would accept God's message.
IBNHISHAM:v1p419/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ولما هلك أبو طالب نالت قريش من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الأذى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r1.claim: The apparent referent of منهم is the Banū Zafar who argued for and defended the Banū Ubayriq; without God's protection and revelation of their concealment, they would have diverted the Prophet from just judgment despite knowing the culprit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r1.anchor: الظاهر: أن الضمير في منهم عائد على بني ظفر المجادلين والذابين عن بني أبيرق. أي: فلولا عصمته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that the verse concerned a delegation from Thaqīf seeking allegiance without conscription or taxes and a year's enjoyment of al-ʿUzzā; when the Prophet declined, it was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r2.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس: أنها نزلت في وفد ثقيف قدموا على الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says God showed His Prophet the degree of his protection and that it came through divine favor and mercy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وفق الله نبيه على مقدار عصمته له، وأنها بفضل من الله ورحمته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān explains that someone among the people might make misleading the Prophet an undertaking, but God's protection thwarts the effort.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r4.anchor: والمعنى: ولولا عصمة الله لك لكان في الناس من يشتغل بإضلالك ويجعله هم نفسه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the first account but qualifies the hypothetical as an attempt that could affect the Prophet, or as an effort to mislead him from religion; divine protection stopped it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r5.anchor: والظاهر القول الأول كما ذكرنا، إلا أن الهم يحتاج إلى قيد أي: لهمت طائفة منهم هما يؤثر عندك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r6.claim: The consequence of colluding in sin, slander, and false testimony falls on the conspirators themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r6.anchor: وبال ما أقدموا عليه من التعاون على الإثم والبهت، وشهادة الزور، إنما هو يخصهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r7.claim: The preposition من explicitly makes the negation universal: they cannot harm the Prophet in any amount, little or great.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r7.anchor: من تدل على العموم نصا أي: لا يضرونك قليلا ولا كثيرا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r8.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r8.claim: Al-Qaffāl reads this as a promise that the Prophet will remain protected in the future.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61/r8.anchor: قال القفال: وهذا وعد بالعصمة في المستقبل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r1.claim: الكتاب means the Qurʾān; the verse's reference to the Prophet receiving the Book and Wisdom and being charged to convey them establishes his protection from error and doubt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r1.anchor: الكتاب: هو القرآن. والحكمة تقدم تفسيرها والمعنى: إن من أنزل الله عليه الكتاب والحكمة وأهله لذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Muqātil identify what the Prophet was taught as the law.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: هو الشرع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r3.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r3.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dimashqī says the phrase means knowledge of the past and future generations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الدمشقي: أخبار الأولين والآخرين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r4.speaker: الماوردي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r4.claim: Al-Māwardī includes the Book and Wisdom and also the measure of the Prophet's own noble worth among the interpretations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r4.anchor: وذكر الماوردي: الكتاب والحكمة، وذكر أيضا مقدار نفسك النفيسة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r5.claim: Another view takes the phrase as hidden matters and the inner thoughts of hearts, knowable only through revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: خفيات الأمور، وضمائر الصدور التي لا يطلع عليها إلا بوحي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r6.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r6.claim: Al-Qaffāl's first possibility is religious knowledge: although the Prophet had not known the Book or faith, God disclosed their secrets and truths, and will continue to guard him from misleading hypocrites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r6.anchor: قال القفال: يحتمل وجهين: أحدهما: أن يراد ما يتعلق بالدين كما قال تعالى: ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r7.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl's second possibility is knowledge of earlier peoples, extended to God's teaching the Prophet about hypocrites' schemes so he can guard against them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r7.anchor: الثاني: ما لم تكن تعلم من أخبار القرون السالفة، فكذلك يعلمك من حيل المنافقين وكيدهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the general sense, encompassing everything the Prophet did not know until God informed him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r8.anchor: والظاهر العموم، فيشمل جميع ما ذكروه. فالمعنى: الأشياء التي لم تكن تعلمها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r9.claim: One interpretation of God's great favor is the gift of faith; Abū Sulaymān says it means what God specially bestowed on the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r9.anchor: قيل: المنة بالإيمان. وقال أبو سليمان: هو ما خصه به تعالى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r10.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r10.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Rāzī calls this proof that knowledge is the noblest virtue: although each person's share of created knowledge is small, God calls it great.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r10.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: هذا من أعظم الدلائل على أن العلم أشرف الفضائل والمناقب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.claim: Across the passage Abū Ḥayyān notes metaphors for traveling and turning toward battle, repetitions with differing complements, and matching or near-matching word forms such as يضلوك وما يضلون and علمك وتعلم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p61#2/r11.anchor: وتضمنت هذه الآيات أنواعا من الفصاحة والبيان والبديع. منها الاستعارة في: وإذا ضربتم في الأرض،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.claim: The phrases بما أراك الله and ما لم تكن تعلم leave their referents unspecified, creating ambiguity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r3.anchor: والإبهام في قوله: بما أراك الله وفي: ما لم تكن تعلم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p62/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes ellipsis at several places across the passage.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r1.claim: God's favor and mercy informed the Prophet through revelation and alerted him to the truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r1.anchor: بإعلامك بماهم عليه بالوحى وتنبيهك على الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r2.claim: One view identifies God's favor as prophethood and His mercy as protection from error.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r2.anchor: وقيل : لولا فضله بالنبوة ورحمته بالعصمة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r3.claim: Another view identifies the favor as prophethood and the mercy as revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r3.anchor: وقيل : لولا فضله بالنبوة ورحمته بالوحى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r4.claim: A further explanation is God's safeguarding and protecting the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r4.anchor: وقيل : المراد لولا حفظه لك وحراسته إياك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r5.claim: The faction can mean Asir ibn Urwa and his associates among those who betrayed the trust.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r5.anchor: والمراد بهم أسير بن عروة وأصحابه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r6.claim: Another identification is those defending Tuʿma who knew the real facts of the case.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r6.anchor: أو الذابون عن طعمة المطلعون على كنه القصة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r7.claim: The pronoun may refer to people generally, with the faction being those who supported the thief or dishonest trustee.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير راجعا إلى الناس والمراد بالطائفة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
