ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that a Thaqif delegation sought a pledge not to break their idols and to worship al-ʿUzza for a year; the Prophet refused, God protected him, and the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنهم قدموا على رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r9.claim: Abu Muslim says the faction was hypocrites who plotted unsuccessfully to destroy the Prophet, whom God guarded.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r9.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم أنهم المنافقون هموا بما لم ينالوا

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r10.claim: They sought to divert the Prophet from judging justly.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r10.anchor: أي بأن يضلوك عن القضاء بالحق

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r11.claim: The phrase may mean diverting him from following the revelation about idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r11.anchor: أو عن اتباع ماجاءك فى أمر الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r12.claim: It may also mean to destroy him; the Qurʾan uses this sense in its question about being lost in the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r12.anchor: أو بأن يهلكوك وقد جاء الإضلال بهذا المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r13.claim: Although only their effect is explicitly negated, the wording denies their intention to signal that their effort had no effect at all.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r13.anchor: وانما نفى همهم مع أن المنفى إنما هو ثأثيره فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r14.claim: Another reading takes this as an effective plot, which in reality could not occur.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r14.anchor: وقيال المراد هو الهم المؤثر ولاريب فى انتفائه حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r15.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r15.claim: Al-Raghib says they were Muslims and did not intend to mislead the Prophet; they believed their action was right.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r15.anchor: وقال الراغب : إن القوم كانوا مسلمين ولم يهموا بإضلاله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r16.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r16.claim: Abu al-Baqa allows an omitted answer to the conditional, estimated as: without God's favor they would have misled you, followed by an independent clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r16.anchor: وجوز أبو البقاء أن يكون الجواب محذوفا والتقدير ولولا فضل الله

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r17.claim: On Abu al-Baqa's parsing, lahamma is an independent resumption meaning they certainly intended it.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r17.anchor: ثم استأنف بقوله سبحانه : لهمت أى لقد همت بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r18.claim: They only turn themselves from the truth, or destroy themselves as the consequences and harm return upon them.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r18.anchor: أى مايزيلون عن الحق إلا أنفسهم أو مايهلكون إلا إياها

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r19.claim: The statement is parenthetical, and the following statement about harming the Prophet is coordinated with it.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r19.anchor: والجملة اعتراضية وقوله تعالى : ( ومايضرونك من شىء ( عطف عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r20.claim: Its coordination with the preceding infinitive phrase is formal only; min is extra, making the phrase an accusative cognate object meaning no harm whatsoever.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r20.anchor: وعطفه على أن يضلوك وهم محض و من صلة والمجرور فى محل النصب

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r21.claim: God preserves the Prophet from error in judgment; any thought he had followed the apparent evidence and the speakers' assurances without knowing the hidden truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r21.anchor: لما أنه تعالى عاصمك عن الزيغ فى الحكم وأما ماخطر ببالك فكان عملا منك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r22.claim: Alternatively, God protects him from appeasing or following the views of heretics against revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r22.anchor: أو لما أنه سبحانه عاصمك عن المداهنة والميل إلى آراء الملحدين

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r23.claim: A further explanation is that God promised to protect him from people and prevent them from reaching him.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r23.anchor: أو لما أنه جل شأنه وعدك العصمة من الناس وحجبهم عن التمكن منك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r24.claim: The book and wisdom together refer to the Qurʾan, which combines both qualities.

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r25.claim: Another view identifies wisdom with the Sunna.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r25.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالحكمة السنة وقد تقدم الكلام فى تحقيق ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r26.speaker: الأجهوري والطبرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r26.claim: Al-Ajhuri, with a similar indication from al-Tabarsi, reads the revelation as the reason for the preceding divine protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r26.anchor: على ما قال الاجهورى : فى موضع التعليل لما قبلها لما قبلها والى ذلك أشار الطبرسى

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r27.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r27.claim: Abu Muslim does not accept that the revelation clause explains the preceding protection clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r27.anchor: وهو غير مسلم على ماذهب اليه أبو مسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r28.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r28.claim: God taught him through kinds of revelation things he had not known, including hidden affairs, inward thoughts, and how to undo hostile schemes.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r28.anchor: وعلمك ( بأنواع الوحى ( مالم تكن تعلم ( أى الذى لم تكن تعلمه من خفيات الأمور

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r29.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r29.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r29.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets the unknown matters as worldly affairs and legal rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r29.anchor: أو من أمور الدنيا وأحكام الشرع كما روى عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r30.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r30.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r30.claim: Al-Dahhak explains the knowledge as what is good and evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r30.anchor: أو من الخير والشر كما قال الضحاك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r31.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r31.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r31.claim: Another explanation is knowledge of reports about earlier and later peoples, or all the listed kinds of knowledge together.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p143/r31.anchor: أو من أخبار الأولين والآخرين كما قيل أو من جميع ماذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r1.claim: Some interpret the object of knowledge as the secrets of the Book and wisdom: God disclosed their mysteries and realities to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r1.anchor: ومن الناس من فسر الموصول بأسرار الكتاب والحكمة أى أنه سبحانه أنزل عليك ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r2.claim: Al-Bahr favors the inclusive sense of the knowledge rather than limiting it to one listed interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r2.anchor: فتكون الجملة الثانية كالتتمة للجملة الأولى واستظهر فى البحر العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r3.claim: God's favor exceeds expression and description; among its instances are universal prophethood, supreme leadership, and the greatest intercession on Resurrection Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v5p144/r3.anchor: لاتحويه عبارة ولاتحيط به إشارة ومن ذلك النبوة العامة والرياسة التامة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r6.claim: The phrase means that a group truly intended to mislead the Prophet; hamma means to intend or resolve.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r6.anchor: يقول للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: {لهمت} لقد همت أي: أضمرت

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r7.claim: The group was Thaʿma’s people, who tried to mislead the Prophet about the ruling and confuse the matter so he would defend Thaʿma.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r7.anchor: يعني: قوم طعمة، {أن يضلوك} يخطئوك في الحكم ويلبسوا عليك الأمر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r8.claim: Their attempt to mislead harms only themselves; its injury returns to them and does not harm the Prophet.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r9.claim: The Book means the Qurʾan, and wisdom means judgment through revelation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r10.claim: One explanation says God taught the Prophet legal rulings he had not known.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r10.anchor: من الأحكام، وقيل: من علم الغيب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p285#3/r11.claim: Another explanation says God taught him knowledge of the unseen.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r5.claim: God’s favor and mercy toward the Messenger took the form of revealing to him what the group was doing; the pronoun refers to the Messenger.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r5.anchor: بإعلام ما هم عليه بالوحي، والضمير لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r6.claim: The group, from Banu Ẓafar, nearly led the Prophet away from right judgment despite knowing the facts; the conditional’s answer denies their success, not their attempt.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r6.anchor: أي من بني ظفر. { أن يضلوك } عن القضاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r7.claim: They mislead only themselves because they did not divert the Prophet from the truth, and the harm returns upon them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r7.anchor: لأنه ما أزلك عن الحق وعاد وباله عليهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r8.claim: God protected the Prophet; his initial thought relied on appearances, not partiality in judgment. “Anything” is an accusative of cognate extent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r8.anchor: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى عصمك وما خطر ببالك كان اعتمادا منك على ظاهر الأمر لا ميلا في الحكم، ومن شيء في موضع النصب على المصدر أي شيء من الضرر

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r9.claim: God taught the Prophet hidden matters or matters of religion and law.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:112-113/r9.anchor: من خفيات الأمور، أو من أمور الدين والأحكام

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:113-114/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:113-114/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:113-114/r1.claim: God’s favor is immense because no favor exceeds prophethood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:113-114/r1.anchor: إذ لا فضل أعظم من النبوة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r7.claim: After warning and directing people in the case, God recounts His favor in protecting the Prophet from their effort to make him argue for the traitor.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r7.anchor: في هذه النازلة وحذر ونهى وأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r8.claim: God's favor is the revelation of the Book, and His mercy is elevating the Prophet's cause and protecting him and his companions from the plot.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r8.anchor: أي بإعلاء أمرك وعصمتك من كل ذي كيد

BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r9.claim: A group tried to mislead the Prophet into clearing Tu'ma; they sought to defend their kinsman without having verified the facts, but God preserved the Prophet.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r9.anchor: وحفظك في أصحابك الذين أتوا يجادلون عن ابنعمهم سارق الدرع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r10.claim: Their effort to mislead would only bring harm on themselves.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r10.anchor: أي على حالة من حالات هذا الهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r11.claim: They can never harm the Prophet by misguidance or otherwise; this promises continuing protection outwardly and inwardly, as also indicated by a verse in al-Ma'ida.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r11.anchor: وهو وعد بدوام العصمة في الظاهر والباطن كآية المائدة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r12.claim: Wisdom is comprehensive understanding of the purposes of the Book, perfecting the Prophet's and his followers' actions and attaining sound knowledge and practice.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p316/r12.anchor: أي الفهم لجميع مقاصد الكتاب فتكون أفعالك وأفعال من تابعك فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r1.claim: God taught the Prophet difficult matters and other things, both unseen and visible, in religious and worldly life.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r1.anchor: أي من المشكلات وغيرها غيبا وشهادة من أحوال الدين والدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r2.claim: God's other favors on the Prophet are beyond enumeration; this verse is among the strongest proofs that knowledge is the noblest virtue.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p317/r2.anchor: وهذا من أعظم الأدلة على أن العلم أشرف الفضائل

DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.claim: Qatada says Banu Ubayriq enlisted Asir ibn Urwa and others to portray the accusation as baseless; the Prophet reproached Qatada, who regretted speaking, then revelation condemned the defense of the traitors and their false accusation of Lubayd.
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r2.anchor: فقالوا: يا رسول الله إن قتادة بن النعمان وعمه عمدوا إلى أهل بيت منا أهل إسلام وصلاح

DURR-FULL:v2p670/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r3.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r3.claim: The account identifies the group who intended to mislead Muhammad as Asir ibn Urwa and his companions, and explains the call to seek forgiveness as concerning what was said to Qatada.
DURR-FULL:v2p670/r3.anchor: {واستغفر الله} أي مما قلت لقتادة {إن الله كان غفورا رحيما ولا تجادل عن الذين يختانون أنفسهم}

DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.claim: In this account, Ta'ma's allies among the Ansar ask Muhammad to defend him and discredit the Jewish accuser; revelation checks that defense, condemns their private plotting, and exposes Ta'ma, who flees to Mecca and apostatizes.
DURR-FULL:v2p675/r1.anchor: من الأنصار فقالوا: يا رسول الله جادل عن طعمة وأكذب اليهودي

DURR-FULL:v2p676/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p676/r1.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p676/r1.claim: In Ikrima's account, the group is Ta'ma's people; the no-good-in-much-secret-talk verse is general, and Ta'ma apostatizes, attempts further thefts, is expelled, and dies stoned after robbing travelers; the account says the verses through 4:116 concern him.
DURR-FULL:v2p676/r1.anchor: طعمة بن أبيرق {ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته} لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم {لهمت طائفة

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r1.claim: The Banū Ubayriq case occasioned this verse; the group who tried to mislead the Prophet is identified as Usayr ibn ʿUrwa and his companions.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r1.anchor: عن أبيه عن جده قتادة بن النعمان وذكر قصة بني ابيرق

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī recounts the Anṣārī who urged them to counsel their companion and argued for him; their action is described as an attempt to mislead the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي ثم ذكر الانصاري واتيناهم اياه ان ينصح عن صاحبهم وجادل عنه فقال : لقد همت طائفة منهم ان يضلوك

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says God taught the Prophet knowledge of this world and the next, including what is lawful and unlawful, so he could use it as proof against creation.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قال : علمه الله بيان الدنيا والاخرة ، بين حلاله وحرامه ، ليحتج بذلك على خلقه

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God taught the Prophet good and evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1064#2/r4.anchor: عن جوبير ، عن الضحاك قال : علمه الخير والشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r1.claim: This clause coordinates with the command not to advocate for the treacherous in 4:105; divine favor here is the revelation that clarifies correct judgment and protects the Prophet from error in it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك } عطف على

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r2.claim: The apparent sense is that the faction’s attempt to mislead the Prophet never even arose, much less succeeded: public knowledge of his honesty prevented them from confidently trying to pass off a lie.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r2.anchor: وظاهر الآية أن هم طائفة من الذين يختانون أنفسهم بأن يضلون الرسول غير واقع من أصله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r3.claim: In one account, Banu Zufr complained to the Prophet about Qatada ibn al-Nuʿman and his uncle while believing Banu Ubayriq were in the right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r3.anchor: وأن بني ظفر لما اشتكوا إليه من صنيع قتادة بن النعمان وعمه كانوا يظنون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, Banu Ubayriq complained about Qatada while fearing that God would disclose the facts to the Prophet; their bid was hopeful, not a firm resolve, since ham implies determination and confidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r4.anchor: أو أن بني أبيرق لما شكوا إلى رسول الله بما صنعه قتادة كانوا موجسين خيفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r5.claim: An alternative takes the verse to deny only the effect of their attempt, meaning God prevented the Prophet from being misled; Ibn ʿAshur rejects this as weak in both wording and meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r5.anchor: وقيل في تفسير هذا الانتفاء : إن المراد انتفاء أثره ، أي لولا فضل الله لضللت بهمهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r6.claim: Any attempted deception would mislead the plotters themselves: they would deserve error for trying to promote falsehood, while the Prophet would not heed it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى : { وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم } أنهم لو هموا بذلك لكان الضلال لاحقا بهم دونك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r7.claim: The preposition min in the denial of harm is augmentative and reinforces the negation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.claim: Shayʾ would originally be accusative as an absolute object meaning “any harm,” but it is genitive because it follows the augmentative preposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r8.anchor: و { شيء } أصله النصب على أنه مفعول مطلق لقوله { يضرونك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.claim: The revelation clause coordinates with the statement that they cannot harm the Prophet, further establishing the earlier divine favor; the final mention of great favor echoes the opening (ring composition).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r9.anchor: وجملة : { وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة } عطف على { وما يضرونك من شيء }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v5p196#2/r10.claim: The Book is the Qurʾan, wisdom is Prophethood, and the knowledge taught beyond the Book includes the Sunna and reports of unseen matters.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.claim: Hammat means that the group would make misleading the Prophet its consuming purpose until it carried it out.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.anchor: لهمت معناه: لجعلته همها وشغلها حتى تنفذه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.claim: The wording is general beyond this case: without God's protection, people would set themselves to mislead the Prophet as these partisans did, but protection defeats their plots and leaves misguidance with them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.anchor: وإلا فأهل التعصب لبني أبيرق قد وقع همهم وثبت، وإنما المعنى: ولولا عصمة الله لك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r1.claim: Through the recited Book and wisdom, God taught the Prophet what he had not known; the remainder of the verse is self-explanatory.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r1.anchor: وبهذين علمه ما لم يكن يعلم، وباقي الآية بين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r2.claim: The Book is the recited revelation; wisdom includes teachings given to the Prophet and a native, cultivated faculty for judging among people, through which he was taught what he did not know and does not speak from whim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p112/r2.anchor: والحكمة التي بعضها خوطب به وبعضها جعلت له سجية ملكها، وقريحة يعمل عنها، وينظر بين الناس بها، لا ينطق عن الهوى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ibn al-Sa'ib, connects the verse to Tu'ma and his people misleading the Prophet about their companion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r1.anchor: هذا قول ابن عباس من طريق ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, says a Thaqif delegation sought exemption from mobilization and taxation and a year's use of al-Uzza; the verse came after the Prophet declined.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r2.anchor: هذا قول ابن عباس في رواية الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r3.claim: One reported meaning of God's favor and mercy is prophethood and protection from error.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r3.anchor: أحدهما النبوة والعصمة والثاني الإسلام والقرآن رويا عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r4.claim: Another reported meaning of God's favor and mercy is Islam and the Qur'an.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r4.anchor: والثاني الإسلام والقرآن رويا عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r5.claim: Muqatil says God clarified Tu'ma's case and, through the Qur'an, turned the Prophet away from believing the traitor; otherwise a group would have misled him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل لولا فضل الله عليك حيث بين لك أمر طعمة وحولك بالقرآن عن تصديق الخائن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r6.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r6.claim: Al-Farra' takes the sense to be that they indeed intended to mislead the Prophet.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r7.claim: Without God's favor and mercy, the group's intended misguidance would have taken effect.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r7.anchor: لولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته لظهر تأثير ما هموا به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r8.claim: One explanation of leading astray is causing an error in judgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r8.anchor: وفي الإضلال قولان أحدهما التخطئة في الحكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r9.claim: Another explanation of leading astray is turning someone away from the truth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r10.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they mislead themselves because they act like the astray, so misguidance returns to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r10.anchor: قال الزجاج وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم لأنهم يعملون عمل الضالين فيرجع الضلال إليهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r11.claim: The Book sent to the Prophet is the Qur'an.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r11.anchor: فأما الكتاب فهو القرآن وفي الحكمة ثلاثة أقوال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas explains wisdom as judgment by revelation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r12.anchor: أحدها القضاء بالوحي قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r13.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r13.claim: Muqatil explains wisdom as the lawful and the forbidden.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r14.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r14.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi explains wisdom as clarifying the Book, inspiration to what is right, and casting a sound answer into the heart.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r14.anchor: والثالث بيان ما في الكتاب وإلهام الصواب وإلقاء صحة الجواب في الروع قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r15.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil identify what the Prophet was taught as the religious law.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r15.anchor: أحدها أنه الشرع قاله ابن عباس ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r16.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r16.claim: Abu Sulayman says the teaching comprised reports about earlier and later peoples.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r16.anchor: والثاني أخبار الأولين والآخرين قاله أبو سليمان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r17.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p196/r17.claim: Al-Mawardi identifies what the Prophet was taught as the Book and wisdom.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas gives one meaning of God's great favor as the favor of faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه المنة بالإيمان والثاني المنة بالنبوة هذان عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies God's great favor as the gift of prophethood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r2.anchor: والثاني المنة بالنبوة هذان عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r3.speaker: أبو سليمان
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r3.claim: Abu Sulayman takes the great favor to include all favors God singled out for the Prophet.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p197/r3.anchor: والثالث أن عام في جميع الفضل الذي خصه الله به قاله أبو سليمان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r1.speaker: قتادة بن النعمان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r1.claim: The report identifies the faction as Usayr b. ʿUrwah and his companions: they praised the Banu Ubairiq and blamed Qatādah for accusing them, although the facts were otherwise, so God clarified the case to the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r1.anchor: عن عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة الأنصاري عن أبيه، عن جده قتادة بن النعمان -وذكر قصة بني أبيرق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r2.claim: God supported and protected Muhammad, gave him the Qur'an and the Sunnah, and taught him what he had not known before revelation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r2.anchor: ثم امتن عليه بتأييده إياه في جميع الأحوال، وعصمته له، وما أنزل عليه من الكتاب، وهو القرآن، والحكمة، وهي السنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r3.claim: The revelation and guidance given to Muhammad are illustrated by the disclosure that he had not known the Book or faith before God made revelation a guiding light and straight path.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r3.anchor: كقوله: {وكذلك أوحينا إليك روحا من أمرنا ما كنت تدري ما الكتاب [ولا الإيمان ولكن جعلناه نورا نهدي به من نشاء من عبادنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r4.claim: God's gift of revelation is also linked to the statement that Muhammad had not expected to receive the Book except through his Lord's mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p410#2/r4.anchor: وقال تعالى: {وما كنت ترجو أن يلقى إليك الكتاب إلا رحمة من ربك}

JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r1.claim: الهم is what one intends or thinks to do; الهمة likewise denotes aspiration, and الهمام is a king of great aspiration.
JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r1.anchor: الهم: ما هممت، وكذلك الهمة. والهمام: الملك العظيم الهمة

JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r2.claim: The root sense of misguidance is destruction by turning away from the path of salvation toward ruin.
JISHUMI:v3p1739#2/r2.anchor: والإضلال: أصله الإهلاك بالعدول عن طريق النجاة إلى طريق الهلاك

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r1.claim: Their attempted misguidance turns no one from truth except themselves; alternatively, they destroy only themselves, so its punishment returns on them while the Prophet is unharmed.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r1.anchor: وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم أي ما يزيلون عن الحق إلا أنفسهم، وقيل: وما يهلكون إلا أنفسهم

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r2.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet through testimony: God guides him and exposes their intentions so he will not grant their request.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r2.anchor: قيل: لا يضرونك بشهادة؛ لأن الله تعالى يسددك في أمورك، ويبين لك ما أضمروا

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r3.claim: A view identifies them as the Thaqif delegation, whose request could not harm the Prophet because God's care kept him from accepting it.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r3.anchor: وقيل: هم وفد ثقيف لم يضروه بما التمسوا؛ لأنه ثبت بلطف الله فلم يجبهم

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r4.claim: Another view says they were hypocrites who intended to assassinate the Prophet, but God protected him.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r4.anchor: وقيل: هم المنافقون هموا بالفتك به فدفع الله عنه

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r5.claim: A further view identifies them as unbelievers who cannot harm the Prophet's religion or erase his prophethood because God supports him.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r5.anchor: وقيل: هم الكافرون لا يضرونك في دينك وإزالة نبوتك؛ لأنه تعالى يؤيدك

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r6.claim: Here the Book is the Qur'an and wisdom is the rulings contained in it.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r6.anchor: قيل: الكتاب: القرآن، والحكمة: ما فيه من الأحكام

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r7.claim: Another view identifies wisdom as the Sunna.

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r8.claim: Their effort to mislead is implausible when God is revealing the Book and teaching the Prophet its rulings.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r8.anchor: وقيل: كيف يضلونك، وهو ينزل عليك الكتاب ويوحي إليك بالأحكام؟!

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r9.claim: What God taught the Prophet includes the laws and religious ordinances.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r9.anchor: وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم قيل: من الشرائع

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r10.claim: Alternatively, God taught him reports about earlier and later peoples and what has been and will be.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r10.anchor: وقيل: من أخبار الأولين والآخرين وما كان وما يكون

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r11.claim: One view says God's favor was great from the Prophet's creation until his mission.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r11.anchor: قيل: فضله عليك - منذ خلقك إلى أن بعثك - عظيم

JISHUMI:v3p1742/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r12.claim: Another view locates its greatness in making him the seal of prophets and master of messengers and giving him intercession and other gifts.
JISHUMI:v3p1742/r12.anchor: وقيل: عظيم حيث جعلك خاتم النبيين وسيد المرسلين، وأعطاك الشفاعة وغيرها

TIRMIDHI:3036/r5.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3036/r5.speaker: الله تعالى
TIRMIDHI:3036/r5.claim: The account connects God’s favor and mercy with protecting the Prophet from the faction’s attempt to mislead him in the Banu Ubayriq case; the revelation exposed their plot and taught him what he had not known.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r1.claim: God’s favor and mercy mean His protection, gracious care, and revelation that exposed the group’s secret.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r1.anchor: أي عصمته وألطافه وما اوحى اليك من الاطلاع على سرهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r2.claim: The group trying to mislead the Prophet is from Banū Ẓafar.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r3.claim: They wanted to turn him from a just ruling although they knew their own man was guilty; some knew the full facts.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r3.anchor: عن القضاء بالحق وتوخي طريق العدل مع علمهم أن الجاني هو صاحبهم فقد روي ان ناسا منهم كانوا يعلمون كنه القصة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r4.claim: Their attempt harms only themselves because its consequences fall back on them.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r5.claim: They do not harm the Prophet: he acted on the outward evidence and had no reason to suspect the facts were otherwise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r5.anchor: لأنك انما عملت بظاهر الحال وما كان يخطر ببالك ان الحقيقة على خلاف ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r6.claim: What the Prophet had not known may be hidden events and people’s inner thoughts, or matters of religion and revealed law.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r6.anchor: من خفيات الأمور وضمائر القلوب أو من امور الدين والشرائع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r7.claim: If the group is Banū Ẓafar, minhum refers to them; another view identifies the group as hypocrites and takes minhum to refer to the people generally.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p597#3/r7.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد بالطائفة بنو ظفر ويرجع الضمير في ( منهم ) إلى الناس وقيل الآية في المنافقين

MUJAHID:v1p173#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p173#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p173#3/r1.claim: Mujahid places the attempt to mislead the Prophet in the case of Ibn Bayriq, who stole an iron coat of mail and blamed an innocent Jew; his associates asked the Prophet to defend him publicly.
MUJAHID:v1p173#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إنا أنزلنا إليك الكتاب بالحق ﴾ إلى قوله ﴿ لهمت طائفة منهم أن يضلوك ﴾ فيما بين ذلك في ابن بيرق سرق درعا من حديد فرمى به يهوديا بريئا

MUQATIL:4:109-113/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r7.claim: God's grace and mercy were His favor of the Quran, which clarified Tuʿma's affair and turned the Prophet away from believing the traitors.
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r7.anchor: يعنى ونعمته بالقرآن حين بين لك أمر طعمة، فحولك عن تصديق الخائنين بالقرآن

MUQATIL:4:109-113/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r8.claim: A group from the traitors' people nearly led the Prophet away from the truth.
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r8.anchor: يقول: لكادت طائفة من قوم الخائنين أن يستنزلوك عن الحق

MUQATIL:4:109-113/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r9.claim: They only lead themselves astray; they cannot diminish or otherwise harm the Prophet, since that is not in their power.
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r9.anchor: يعنى وما ينقصونك من شىء ليس ذلك بأيديهم

MUQATIL:4:109-113/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r10.claim: The Book and Wisdom mean the lawful and the unlawful.
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r10.anchor: ثم قال: { وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب والحكمة } ، يعنى الحلال والحرام

MUQATIL:4:109-113/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r11.claim: God taught the Prophet what he had not known about scripture and religion.
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r11.anchor: { وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم } من أمر الكتاب وأمر الدين

MUQATIL:4:109-113/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r12.claim: The great favor bestowed on the Prophet is prophethood and the Book.
MUQATIL:4:109-113/r12.anchor: { وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما } [آية: 113]، يعنى النبوة والكتاب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r1.claim: God’s favor and mercy protected the Prophet and kept him from discovering the conspirators’ secret.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r1.anchor: أى عصمته ولطفه من الاطلاع على سرهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r2.claim: The group may be some of Banū Ẓafar or all of them; «them» may refer to people generally.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r2.anchor: من بنى ظفر أو المراد بالطائفة بنو ظفر والضمير فى منهم يعود إلى الناس

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r3.claim: They sought to divert him from judging justly although they knew their own man was guilty.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r3.anchor: عن القضاء بالحق وتوخى طريق العدل مع علمهم بأن الجانى صاحبهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r4.claim: Their attempted deception would bring harm only upon themselves.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r5.claim: They could not harm the Prophet because he acted on outward facts and did not know the truth was otherwise.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r5.anchor: لأنك إنما عملت بظاهر الحال وما كان يخطر ببالك أن الحقيقة على خلاف ذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r6.claim: The Book is the Qurʾān and Wisdom is the Sunna.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r7.claim: What God taught may mean religious matters and laws, or hidden matters and the secrets within hearts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r7.anchor: من أمور الدين والشرائع أو من خفيات الأمور وضمائر القلوب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p248/r8.claim: God’s favor was great in what He taught the Prophet and bestowed upon him.

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r1.claim: God's favor and mercy here mean protection: a party of Banu Zafar defending Tu'ma intended to mislead the Prophet from a just judgment by disguising the facts.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r1.anchor: {ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته} بالعصمة {لهمت طآئفة منهم} أي من بني ظفر وهم الذابون عن طعمة

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r2.claim: The wording does not deny that they intended to mislead the Prophet; it denies that their effort had any effect on him.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r2.anchor: وليس القصد فيه إلى نفي همهم بل إلى نفي تأثيره

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r3.claim: Their misguidance harms only themselves because its consequence falls back on them.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r3.anchor: {وما يضلون إلا أنفسهم} لأن وبالهم عليهم

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r4.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet at all because God protects him; his passing thought relied on outward appearances and was not bias in judgment.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r4.anchor: {وما يضرونك من شىء} محل الجار والمجرور النصب على المصدرية

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r5.claim: The Book is the Qur'an, and the wisdom is its legal rulings, through which God taught what is lawful and unlawful.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r5.anchor: {وأنزل الله عليك الكتاب} أي القرآن {والحكمة} أي ما في القرآن من الأحكام

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r6.claim: God taught the Prophet unseen and hidden matters through revelation, things he had not known before that teaching.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r6.anchor: {وعلمك} بالوحي من الغيب وخفيات الأمور {ما لم تكن تعلم} ذلك إلى وقت التعليم

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r7.claim: The great favor includes universal prophethood and complete leadership, along with God's protection and teaching.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك الفضل العظيم عصمته وتعليمه ما لم يعلم

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r8.claim: The author reports al-Haddadi's ruling that nobody may advocate for another to establish or deny a right without knowing the facts.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r8.anchor: وفي هذه الآيات دلالة أنه لا يجوز لأحد أن يخاصم لغيره في إثبات حق أو نفيه غير عالم بحقيقة أمره

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r9.claim: The author reports al-Haddadi's rule that a judge may not favor one litigant over another, even when one is Muslim and the other a non-Muslim.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r9.anchor: أنه لا يجوز للحاكم الميل إلى أحد الخصمين وإن كان أحدهما مسلما والآخر كافرا

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r10.claim: The author reports al-Haddadi's ruling that possession of stolen property alone does not require judgment that its holder stole it.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r10.anchor: وأن وجود السرقة في يدي إنسان لا يوجب الحكم بها عليه

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r11.speaker: الصائب
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r11.claim: The author says evil's consequence returns to its perpetrator, just as good benefits its doer; al-Sa'ib's poem illustrates that the oppressor first suffers the effect of his injustice.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r11.anchor: قال الصائب : أول بظالمان أثر ظلم ميرسد يش از هدف هميشه كمان ناله ميكند

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r12.claim: A tale says God dried the hand of a man slaughtering a calf before its mother, then restored it when a bird's chick returned from its nest to its mother; the saying warns against selling people, cutting trees, or slaughtering cattle.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r12.anchor: حكي أن الله تعالى أيبس يد رجل يذبح عجل بقرة بين يدي أمه ثم ردها برد فرخ سقط من وكره إلى أمه

BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r13.claim: A woman gave a morsel to a beggar; later a wolf took her child, and God returned the child unharmed, explaining that the rescue answered the morsel she had given.
BURSEVI:v2p225#2/r13.anchor: حكي أن امرأة وضعت لقمة في فم سائل ثم ذهبت إلى مزرعة فوضعت ولدها في موضع فأخذه الذئب

BURSEVI:v2p226/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r1.claim: Knowledge and wisdom are among the greatest virtues, especially beneficial knowledge that brings a person nearer to God; the Prophet's prayer seeks refuge from knowledge that does not benefit.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r1.anchor: ومنها أن العلم والحكمة من أعظم الفضائل والمراد العلم النافع المقرب إلى الله تعالى أعاذنا الله مما لم ينفع منه

BURSEVI:v2p226/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r2.claim: The author cites the Prophet's prayer for refuge from knowledge that brings no benefit.

BURSEVI:v2p226/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v2p226/r3.claim: Muslim transmits from Abu Hurayra that a person's deeds cease at death except for ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for them.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r3.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه

BURSEVI:v2p226/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r4.claim: A servant should attribute every virtue to God's favor and mercy rather than praise the self; self-admiration dims inward lights of certainty, and even a lifetime of deeds cannot repay the gift of existence.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r4.anchor: ومنها أن لا يرى العبد الفضائل والخيرات من نفسه بل من فضل الله ورحمته وليس للعبد أن يزكي نفسه

BURSEVI:v2p226/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r5.speaker: شاه شعاع الكرماني
BURSEVI:v2p226/r5.claim: Shah Shuja al-Kirmani offered to trade fifty years of pilgrimage for a single good deed given to a poor man; when a jurist accused him of slighting the law, he said he saw no value in himself or his deeds.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r5.anchor: حكي عن شاه شعاع الكرماني أنه كان جالسا في مسجد فقام فقير وسأل الناس فلم يعطوه شيئا فقال الكرماني من يشتري حج خمسين سنة

BURSEVI:v2p226/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r6.claim: Humility about deeds does not mean abandoning work: people should perform every good act without valuing it, seeing their ability and success as God's enabling grace.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r6.anchor: وليس المراد التعطيل عن العمل بل يعملون جميع الحسنات ولا يرون لها قدرا بل يرون التوفيق لها من فضل الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v2p226/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r7.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v2p226/r7.claim: Al-Sa'di's verse says any good that reaches another person comes through God's enabling grace, so the servant should praise God and not regard himself.

BURSEVI:v2p226/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r8.claim: Divine favor is a gift from God, not something a servant can earn or attract; it guides a servant to faith and enables righteous action.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r8.anchor: والإشارة في الآية أن فضل الله موهبة من مواهب الحق يؤتيه من يشاء وليس لأحد فيه مدخل بالكسب والاستجلاب

BURSEVI:v2p226/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r9.claim: The author interprets the great favor as God Himself, who is the Prophet's favor and mercy to the worlds, and cites the saying that the heavens were created for him.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r9.anchor: والعظيم في قوله : {وكان فضل الله عليك عظيما} هو الله تعالى أي أن الله العظيم هو فضل الله عليك ورحمته

BURSEVI:v2p226/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r10.claim: The author cites the saying, 'Were it not for you, I would not have created the spheres,' as a report of the Prophet's immense favor.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r10.anchor: كما أنك فضل الله ورحمته على العالمين

BURSEVI:v2p226/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p226/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p226/r11.claim: Part of God's favor was that nothing spiritual or bodily diverted the Prophet from the path of arrival; the author prays for protection from outward and inward obstacles and union with holy souls.
BURSEVI:v2p226/r11.anchor: ومن فضل الله عليك أنه لم يضله شيء من الروحانيات والجسمانيات عن طريق الوصول اللهم احفظنا من الموانع في طريق الوصول إليك آفاقية أو أنفسية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r1.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r1.claim: Sībawayh says the clause after لولا is a nominative subject whose predicate is omitted and understood.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r1.anchor: ما بعد «لولا» مرفوع بالابتداء عند سيبويه، والخبر محذوف لا يظهر

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r2.claim: God’s favor and mercy mean that He alerted the Prophet to the truth; another explanation is prophethood and protection from error.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r2.anchor: والمعنى: { ولولا فضل الله عليك ورحمته } بأن نبهك على الحق، وقيل: بالنبوءة والعصمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r3.claim: A group tried to mislead the Prophet by asking him to clear Ibn Ubayriq and shift the accusation onto a Jew; God exposed the matter to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r3.anchor: لأنهم سألوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يبرىء ابن أبيرق من التهمة ويلحقها اليهودي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r4.claim: Their effort only misleads themselves: they act like the astray, and the consequences return upon them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r4.anchor: لأنهم يعملون عمل الضالين، فوباله لهم راجع عليهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r5.claim: They cannot harm the Prophet because he is protected from error.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r5.anchor: { وما يضرونك من شيء } لأنك معصوم.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r6.claim: One parsing starts “God sent down the Book and wisdom” as a new sentence; another takes the waw as circumstantial, so they cannot harm him while revelation is sent down.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r6.anchor: هذا ابتداء كلام. وقيل: الواو للحال،

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r7.claim: For the circumstantial reading, the author compares the construction to Imruʾ al-Qays’s line about setting out while birds remain in their nests.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r8.claim: Here wisdom means judgment through revelation.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r9.claim: What God taught the Prophet includes the laws and rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r9.anchor: { وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم } يعني من الشرائع والأحكام.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r10.claim: تعلم is accusative as the predicate of كان; its final vowel is omitted for jussive mood and the waw drops where two sukūns meet.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:113/r10.anchor: { تعلم } في موضع نصب لأنه خبر كان. وحذفت الضمة من النون للجزم، وحذفت الواو لالتقاء الساكنين.

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r1.claim: God's favor means prophethood and His mercy means protection from error; without these, Ta'ma's faction would have led the Prophet into a false judgment.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r1.anchor: أن الله خصك بالفضل وهو النبوة ، وبالرحمة وهي العصمة

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r2.claim: Ta'ma's people knew he was the thief but asked the Prophet to argue for his innocence and attribute the theft to the Jew.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r2.anchor: قوم طعمة كانوا قد عرفوا أن سارق

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r3.claim: Here “lead you astray” means to draw the Prophet into a false, mistaken ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r3.anchor: ومعنى يضلوك أي يلقوك في الحكم الباطل الخطأ

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r4.claim: Their collusion in sin and aggression and their false testimony make them, rather than the Prophet, the ones acting in error.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r4.anchor: بسبب تعاونهم على الإثم والعدوان وشهادتهم بالزور والبهتان

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r5.claim: Al-Qaffal reads this as a promise of future protection: God will continue to guard the Prophet from their attempts to involve him in falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r5.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : وما يضرونك في المستقبل

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r6.claim: On the other reading, their efforts cause no harm because the Prophet did not fall into error: he based his judgment on the apparent evidence, as commanded.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r6.anchor: فأنت ما وقعت في الباطل ، لأنك بنيت الأمر على ظاهر الحال

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r7.claim: If “no harm” promises future protection, the revelation of scripture and the charge to convey law confirm that divine wisdom will protect the messenger from doubt and misguidance.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r7.anchor: فكيف يليق بحكمته أن لا يعصمك عن الوقوع في الشبهات والضلالات

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r8.claim: If the Prophet was excused for judging by appearances, the revealed law itself requires judgments from outward evidence, so doing so cannot harm him.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r8.anchor: وأوجب فيها بناء أحكام الشرع على الظاهر فكيف يضرك بناء الأمر على الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r9.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r9.claim: Al-Qaffal's first reading concerns religious knowledge: God disclosed the scripture's and wisdom's secrets and realities despite the Prophet's earlier lack of that knowledge, and will likewise protect him from future deception.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32/r9.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : هذه الآية تحتمل وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal's second reading is that God taught the Prophet the histories of earlier peoples and will teach him the hypocrites' schemes so he can guard against them.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r1.anchor: الوجه الثاني : أن يكون المراد : وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم من أخبار الأولين

RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r2.claim: The verse shows the great honor of knowledge: human knowledge is only a little, yet God calls this little knowledge great, while calling the world's entire provision little.
RAZI-FULL:v11p32#2/r2.anchor: وهذا من أعظم الدلائل على أن العلم أشرف الفضائل والمناقب
